f_ir.name: loss_advantage_logsigmoid_pairwise_v1
f_ir.intuition: The original candidate was too similar to an existing loss that clamps the margin difference and multiplies by advantage_gap, resulting in a novelty gate failure. To improve novelty and enforce a smooth margin-based loss consistent with preference learning theory, I replaced the hard clamp with a logsigmoid on the difference of log probabilities (log_prob_w - log_prob_l). This smooths the margin and bounds the loss, leveraging the advantage_gap as a multiplier and optional weighting. This design uses a pairwise margin formulation underpinning binary preference likelihood and aligns with configured advantage signals. It still meets hard constraints by using only allowed ops (sub, logsigmoid, mul, mean) and accesses only expected keys.
f_ir.pseudocode:
adv = batch['advantage_gap']
lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
margin = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
score = ops.logsigmoid(margin)
weighted = ops.mul(score, adv)
if weight is not None:
  weighted = ops.mul(weighted, weight)
return ops.mean(weighted)
f_ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    adv = batch['advantage_gap']
    weight = batch.get('weight', None)

    margin = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    score = ops.logsigmoid(margin)
    loss = ops.mul(score, adv)
    if weight is not None:
        loss = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    return ops.mean(loss)
f_ir.theoretical_basis: This loss models the negative log-likelihood of the preferred action winning under a pairwise logistic preference model, with advantage_gap scaling the margin contribution. The logsigmoid provides a smooth, differentiable, and bounded surrogate loss encouraging the model to assign higher log probability to the winning action. Using mean aggregation provides stable scalar feedback per batch.
